Source A1 verified via archived hashes. Original unchanged incident included among preservation controls and historical failing pre-a1 runs are retained separately. No live replay; original Graph success checked event existence/start; per-inbox delivery and later editor identity remain unverified. Direct legacy fixture contexts carry the declared unframed literal as currentUserMessage. Orchestrated turns receive an explicit empty typedUserMessage if no typed source is available. Core, actual connector and resolver boundaries have distinct executed fixtures. Matching pre-fix original and rejected a1 are retained; external human delivery and later editor identity remain outside these checks. Bouncer original partial-edit fixture before/after: artifacts/workshop-verification/incident-20261111/matchmaker/a3/independent-before.tap and artifacts/workshop-verification/incident-20261111/matchmaker/a3/independent-after.tap, the original product fail switches from a POST to internal Alex to a POST to approved external Alex. Earlier before/after records retain their attempt labels; the final package runs current tests on the exact snapshot. This is fixture POST serialization, not inbox receipt. A4 supersedes older expectations that a free-prose email or a tool-only guessed address can be silently substituted. A deliberately entered named mailbox or standalone, uniquely bound mailbox can select a different recipient. Mixed text, multiple unresolved candidates, framed-only suggestions and conflicting tool input now ask before Graph. A fresh name-only allowed change still resolves through the ordinary directory. Historical attempt outcomes are preserved above. Frozen Bouncer before and after artifacts/workshop-verification/incident-20261111/matchmaker/a4/original-before.tap and artifacts/workshop-verification/incident-20261111/matchmaker/a4/original-after.tap: provider serialized the old address on a3, empty on a4. Production delivery and editor identity are unverified; transport is isolated on all reproductions.
